extractedSnippet: SLASH: Sustainable Lands and Safer Homes Last Content Update: Last month SLASH Updates: Blue Mountain Opens Sept 17 : The Blue Mountain Rotational SLASH Yard (23401 Coal Creek Canyon Rd, Arvada) opens Sept 17 and expected to be open Thursdays-Sundays until Sept 27. Reminder: SLASH Yards can close at any time due to capacity or weather. Sign up for SLASH Alerts to be notified of yard closures! ONLY CLEAN MATERIALS WILL BE ACCEPTED, and Pine Needles must be separated from slash. Please see "Materials List" below for more information. To protect staff and equipment, all materials brought to every slash yard MUST be clean of trash, debris, rocks, and yard waste. Pine needles and slash must be separated. Failure to follow these rules will result in being turned away. WE'VE GOT MULCH: Residents can now self-load mulch for FREE from the Tincup Ridge SLASH Yard (101 Rooney Rd.) during normal collection hours. What is Slash? Slash is debris from nature, such as tree limbs, prunings, and pine cones. If not removed, slash can add to potential fire hazards on your property. The importance of mitigating and preparing your property for wildfire cannot be overstated - and again this year, Jefferson County is your partner in this effort. This program is for residents only, though you do not need to be a JeffCo resident to participate.
